headline: Government considers a defence spending freeze
description: Reinmetall says this is probably a spreadsheet error. Investors are checking the defence budget.

quip.text: Defence budgets and I go way back. Mostly back. Away from me, quickly.

headline: Defence budget frozen; tanks told to carpool
description: Reinmetall warns that contracts will be delayed. Its spokesperson suggests waiting for the next budget meeting.

headline: Government discovers that carpooling tanks also costs money
description: Procurement admits the carpool lane needs "a lot of lane". Orders are quietly unfrozen.

headline: Candidate promises free pizza for every voter
description: Polls surge. Economists ask where the pizza will come from. The candidate says "a farm, probably".

quip.text: Free pizza? I would simply own the farm. Already do. Do you?

headline: Pizza Act passes: one pizza per citizen per week
description: Wheat, tomatoes and cheese ministries report a "sudden and delicious" demand spike.

headline: Euro leaders spend six hours debating the font on new banknotes
description: Comic Sans lost by a single vote. Currency traders describe the mood as "typographically uncertain".

headline: Parliament funds "a rocket, any rocket"
description: The bill specifies no destination, no payload and no return date. Aerospace lobbyists are weeping with joy.

quip.text: I looked at MOO years ago. Told you. Several times. You were holding a sandwich.

headline: Cheese war: neighbours build wall to stop "cheese tourism"
description: Farmers fear export chaos. Switzerland quietly declares itself "neutral, but fondue-ready".

headline: Cheese wall dismantled; both sides keep the cheese
description: Negotiators call it "a gouda deal". Exports resume immediately.

headline: Leaders agree on lasting peace, then argue about seating
description: The peace treaty is fine. The seating plan is "the real conflict". Defence stocks wobble on the actual agreement.

headline: Election recount finds 4 million extra votes, all for the moose
description: The moose has not commented. Currency markets approve of the stability.

headline: Two nations declare war over a disputed parking spot
description: Both armies are "extremely serious" and both parked in the same place. Defence and energy stocks surge; gold pays the price of fear.

quip.text: Wars come, wars go. Defence stocks stay. Like my back pain.

headline: War ends: the parking spot was a loading zone
description: Both sides were fined. Defence stocks give back everything and some more.

headline: Navy of 40,000 pigeons blockades the strait
description: Oil tankers are asked to "please stop making that noise". Crude prices lift off.

headline: Pigeons unionise, demand breadcrumbs; strait reopens
description: A deal is struck: bread on Fridays. Tankers sail again.

headline: Superpowers settle border dispute by chess; one side cheats
description: Observers note that nobody has seen a bishop move like that. Safe havens and weapons makers perk up.

headline: Embargo declared on socks; "we can hear the sandals"
description: Footwear diplomacy escalates. Defence contractors report "unusually motivated" procurement.

headline: Frost hits coffee belt; baristas declare national emergency
description: Prices of beans soar as cafes ration "one existential crisis per customer".

quip.text: Honey, are you buying coffee? Or are you buying coffee??

headline: Oil found under national park; nature objects politely
description: The park ranger asked it to stop. The oil company drilled anyway. Crude drops on a supply glut.

headline: OPEC meeting rumoured to be "just a very long brunch"
description: Nobody knows what was decided, but the menu was reportedly "restrictive".

quip.text: Brunch decisions are the best decisions. I once bought a boat at brunch.

headline: OPEC cuts output by "a lot"
description: Exact figures were left off the napkin. The oil market takes this seriously anyway.

headline: Billionaire buys gold to feel something
description: His therapist suggested a hobby. He appears to have misunderstood the assignment.

headline: Therapist: "not that kind of hobby"; billionaire dumps gold
description: He has taken up pottery instead. Gold slips back down the hill.

headline: Phone makers discover silver is shiny, add "Shiny Mode"
description: Demand for the metal surges as every device now needs "at least a bit of sparkle".

headline: Drought: farmers reportedly "praying to each other"
description: Crop yields collapse. Farm stocks surge on scarcity; bakers describe the mood as "crumbly".

headline: Cows sign pledge to stop burping by 2030
description: Environmental groups celebrate. Farm balance sheets, however, show "a lot of unburped optimism".

headline: Silver mine floods; miners declare it "a pool"
description: Output halts while the pool is "enjoyed responsibly". Silver supply tightens.

headline: New flu "Mondayitis" spreads; offices shut for "mild cases"
description: Symptoms include staring at the wall and requesting coffee. Pharma and coffee demand rise.

headline: Placebo Pharma to reveal results of "it works if you believe" trial
description: Analysts will announce the results shortly. Several analysts say they "believe they will".

quip.text: I believe. I believe very hard. Mostly in free samples.

headline: Regulators approve belief-based medicine
description: The pill works for everyone who is told it works. Placebo Pharma stock lifts off.

headline: Rumour: Placebo Pharma's miracle pill may be "just sugar"
description: Company says the rumour is "baseless, but sweet". Insiders say the pharmacy smells of caramel.

headline: Confirmed: it's sugar, "but a very effective sugar"
description: Regulators are not amused. Shares crash as customers ask for "the other kind".

headline: BMUU recalls 400,000 cars: blinker fluid shortage
description: Drivers report that they "never knew there was blinker fluid, and now we are all worried".

headline: BMUU launches blinker subscription at $19.99 a month
description: Customers may now rent the right to turn left. Analysts call it "genius, evil, and genius".

quip.text: Subscription blinkers? I own three. Two for the weekend.

headline: HypeLoop CEO tweets nothing but a pair of eyes for three hours
description: Millions speculate on what he is looking at. HypeLoop shares float upward on pure suspense.

headline: HypeLoop CEO: "It was a typo. I meant eyeglasses."
description: Investors feel personally betrayed. The CEO follows up with a single broken heart.

headline: Moonshot Aerospace: next launch "Tuesday. Or Thursday. Or Mars."
description: The countdown clock reads "ish". Space enthusiasts are cautiously screaming.

quip.text: I was at a launch once. Great hot dogs. Terrible rocket.

headline: Moonshot rocket reaches orbit and returns with a parking ticket
description: The Moon Bureau of Parking is "unimpressed, but billing".

headline: Moon Bureau of Parking sends Moonshot a very large invoice
description: Moonshot calls it "a rounding error with ambitions". Shares give back part of the rally.

headline: Down to Earth Farms caught labelling rocks as "organic"
description: Customers say the rocks were "firm, but not very juicy". Shares plunge. The company promises to "regroup, replant and rebrand".

quip.text: Panic sells. Patience pays. That is the whole business model. Plus bagels.

headline: ClosedAI promises a model that understands printer errors
description: Investors are thrilled by the prospect of "finally understanding PC LOAD LETTER".

headline: Users report that the model has itself become the printer error
description: Support tickets are answered with "PC LOAD LETTER". The share price is not coping.

headline: Macrohard update removes the Update button
description: Users now have no way to update the update. The company says this is "a feature".

headline: AlphaBett: "We are now a bank, a dentist, and a cloud"
description: Analysts cannot decide whether it is brilliant or a cry for help. The market buys it anyway.

headline: Global chip shortage: toasters now require tokens
description: Carmakers and tech giants report that "the little squares are mostly gone".

headline: Parliament bans AI from writing parliament speeches
description: The AI speeches were "too coherent". AI stocks wobble; the vote passes unanimously.

headline: Rumour: AlphaBett quantum chip is "simultaneously working and not working"
description: The lab says it is "probably both". Nobody will open the box.

headline: Observed: the AlphaBett quantum chip works. Probably.
description: The scientists opened the box. The cat is "inconclusively fine". AlphaBett soars.

headline: Data centre cooled by one very old fan catches fire
description: Cloud customers are asked to "please stop uploading memes". AI and tech stocks tumble.

headline: Teenagers discover "phone calls"; social media usage plummets
description: Parents panic as their children say "hello" out loud. HypeLoop stock sags.

headline: NotRugpullCoin team posts "We're definitely staying" from a beach
description: Photos show a yacht, cocktails and a laptop displaying "Treasury: 0.00". The price rallies on pure trust.

quip.text: I tripled my money in NRC. Then I bought a boat. Boat is also NRC.

headline: NotRugpullCoin team "on a long vacation" with the treasury
description: The founders cannot be reached, the website now sells yoga mats, and the coin collapses.

headline: Celebrity dog appears in crypto ad; WoofCoin barks
description: The dog does not appear to know what crypto is. Investors do not care. WoofCoin goes to the moon.

headline: Celebrity dog denies knowing what crypto is
description: "Woof," said the dog, in a statement. WoofCoin reverses violently.

headline: Bitcorn banned in country with no internet
description: Regulators insist the ban is "extremely effective". Crypto traders panic anyway.

headline: Bitcorn ETF approved after a single fax
description: Wall Street calls it "mature". Crypto Twitter calls it "wen moon". Prices jump.

headline: Man finds 4 million Bitcorn on old laptop; city demands 40%
description: Selling pressure fears hit the market. The man says he will "sell slowly, probably".

headline: Bitcorn "halving" party: investors stock up in advance
description: Supply shrinks in a few days. Someone brought half a cake.

headline: Halving complete: nobody understands it, everyone cheers
description: The party ended with "half the guests and double the hype". Bitcorn surges.

headline: Tiny nation replaces gold standard with the banana standard
description: Gold traders feel "peeled". Banana-adjacent farm stocks celebrate.

headline: Meme cat gets its own IPO; investors confuse it with HypeLoop
description: Several brokers report buying "the wrong cat". Social media stocks and meme coins pop.

headline: Parliament votes to cancel Mondays
description: Coffee sellers shudder as one fifth of the demand disappears at once.

headline: Mondays reinstated after nobody could find Tuesday
description: The week resumed with "maximum chaos and caffeine". Coffee surges.

headline: Switzerland adds a 25th hour to catch up on punctuality
description: Swiss clocks now chime "later, but exactly". The franc is a safe bet.

headline: Gouda prices triple; central bank accepts "a wheel" as collateral
description: The euro blinks. Farmers suspect they are "sitting on a gold mine, but with holes".

headline: Llama escapes petting zoo, rings opening bell; stocks sprint
description: No one can explain the rally, but everyone is "extremely llama-positive".

headline: Study: every meeting could have been an email
description: The economy saves 4 billion hours overnight. Productivity software vendors celebrate quietly, by email.

headline: Central bank announces an announcement about interest rates
description: The announcement will be made "soon", "ish" and "in a tone". Traders position themselves nervously.

quip.text: Rate cuts are like free pizza. Everybody smiles. Then the bill.

headline: Rates cut: markets confused but excited
description: Nobody knows why, but cheap money makes stocks sprint. Gold approves. The euro does not.

headline: ECB sets interest rates by group-chat poll
description: The poll was 5 to 4 with two abstentions and one thumbs-up emoji. Euro sinks; franc rises.

headline: Bank of Japan "takes a nap" on yield curve control
description: Markets note that nothing is being controlled. The yen drifts lower.

headline: Bank of Japan wakes up, sees chart, panics
description: An emergency meeting is called. Coffee is served. The yen rockets higher.

headline: Market panic: someone coughed during the opening bell
description: Stocks tumble. Gold, franc and yen climb as nervous money runs for cover.

headline: Market recovers: it was just allergies
description: A spokesperson blames "pollen and drama". Stocks rebound; safe havens fade.

headline: Investor mood declared "immaculate vibes"
description: A survey finds 100% of respondents "feel great and have no data". Stocks and crypto rise, gold yawns.

headline: Swiss National Bank finds 4 tons of gold in grandmother's couch
description: The grandmother wants "finder's fees and tea". Gold supply swells; the franc is proud.

headline: Drump wants to blow up Mount Rushmore: "Room for one more face"
description: The US leader calls the monument "a renovation opportunity". Reinmetall investors hear the word explosives and stop listening to the rest of the speech.

headline: Chinese hackers leak BMUU technology ahead of its unveiling
description: The leaked blueprint shows two wheels and an unusually confident marketing budget. BMUU calls the design "revolutionary" and asks everyone to wait for the launch.

headline: BMUU unveils two-wheeled car that is "definitely not a bike"
description: Executives demonstrate the optional pedal package and insist the handlebar is a steering innovation. Investors are overjoyed; BMUU opens orders for a market debut in four days.

headline: BMUU two-wheeled car misses sales targets; customers buy bikes
description: The market debut sells three units, two to the marketing department. Investors are surprised that a bicycle with a car payment is a difficult pitch. BMUU shares crash as the board promises a relaunch.

headline: Melon Musk tweets: "NRC is going to the moon"
description: NotRugpullCoin traders buy before checking whether Melon means the coin, a rocket or his new nightclub. The tweet contains no further details and twelve rocket emojis.

headline: NotRugpullCoin creator "Asuspicous Per Son" reportedly sells everything
description: The founder calls the empty treasury "a decentralised absence of funds". NotRugpullCoin collapses as investors discover the suspicious part was the entire person.

headline: ClosedAI promises a huge leap in AI-driven robots at upcoming convention
description: The invitation says the demonstration will "flip your expectations". ClosedAI investors start buying ahead of the convention in three days.

headline: ClosedAI robot manages only three backflips; investors wanted four
description: The robot completes three perfect backflips, then requests a software update and a chair. The audience calls it a technological disappointment. ClosedAI shares tumble over the next two days.

headline: Russia's Butin reportedly sends containers of vodka to AlphaBett headquarters
description: AlphaBett reception signs for "office supplies". Investors worry that the next product roadmap will be written on a cocktail napkin; shares slip slightly.

headline: Macrohard unveils Windows Classic; investors buy the nostalgic feeling
description: The launch promises the comfort of an older operating system with the confidence of a modern price tag. Macrohard shares rise while reviewers wait three days for their copies to finish installing.

headline: Windows Classic turns out to be the 1998 operating system
description: Reviewers find no new features, the original bugs and a help wizard who refuses to retire. Macrohard insists that "unchanged" is a premium nostalgia feature. Investors disagree.

headline: Cheese trade tensions rise between the Netherlands and Germany
description: Border guards demand documentation for every slice. Both governments describe the situation as "mature but escalating". Reinmetall receives inquiries about armoured cheese transport.

headline: Local grandma declares total war on upstairs party-makers
description: After a third sleepless night, she announces a defence budget and a strict no-bass doctrine. Reinmetall investors refuse to underestimate a woman holding a rolling pin.

headline: Postal services say AlphaBett navigation routes every van to ice cream shops
description: Parcel deliveries are late, but driver satisfaction has never been higher. Major postal customers threaten to cancel their navigation contracts; AlphaBett shares slide.

headline: Rumour: ClosedAI develops model exceptionally good at identifying squirrels
description: The model distinguishes squirrels from slightly different squirrels with astonishing accuracy. ClosedAI investors struggle to identify a customer and begin questioning what they have funded.

headline: Squirrels carrying incurable disease escape laboratory; UN offers tracking bounty
description: The UN urgently needs a company that can find the escaped squirrels. ClosedAI announces that its suspiciously specific model is ready. Investors discover a market for squirrel identification at remarkable speed.

headline: Macrohard CEO spotted bench-pressing 200 kg at local gym
description: Analysts upgrade Macrohard from "solid fundamentals" to "absolutely massive fundamentals". Investors pile in after a photo proves the CEO can, literally, lift the company.

headline: Football star kicks ball into space: "Just kick something really hard"
description: The striker claims rockets are an unnecessary subscription. Investors question Moonshot Aerospace's entire business model after the club offers orbital deliveries with every season ticket.

headline: Chinese-made pet drones turn daily walks into "air walks"
description: Dogs get a view, cats file complaints, and every pet owner suddenly wants lift-off. Moonshot Aerospace announces plans to supply flight systems as investors discover the low-altitude pet economy.

headline: BMUU CEO takes submarine car to the Titanic to prove its capabilities
description: The CEO calls deep-sea pressure "a branding challenge" and promises a live demonstration in three days. Investors cheer BMUU's expansion into a market with almost no traffic.

headline: BMUU CEO reportedly killed as submarine car implodes during Titanic expedition
description: Investigators say the vehicle's depth rating was listed as "optimistic". BMUU shares collapse as the board suspends the submarine-car programme and announces a safety overhaul.

headline: All major US supermarket chains accept NotRugpullCoin as payment
description: Retailers describe the coin as "extremely safe" and "trustworthy", citing its name as their main due-diligence document. NotRugpullCoin surges as shoppers prepare to pay for groceries with reassurance.

headline: Billionaire spends entire fortune on gold because "the colour is pretty"
description: Asked about diversification, the billionaire requests a second shade of gold. The enormous purchase sends gold prices sharply higher and interior designers into a bidding war.

headline: Middle Eastern strongman Warpin vows to bomb coffee plantations in three days
description: After one bitter espresso, Warpin declares that "the beans must answer for this". Reinmetall and coffee traders watch the three-day ultimatum, but prices have not reacted yet.

headline: Fifty coffee plantations hit overnight after Warpin's bitter-coffee ultimatum
description: Reinmetall shares rise on fresh orders. Coffee buyers cancel contracts over fears of further attacks and disrupted shipments; a panic sell-off sends coffee prices falling over the next two days.

headline: Leaked memo: Swiss minister will swap half the franc reserves for cheese
description: An insider forwards a memo scheduling the conversion in three days. The minister's entire written justification is "I love cheese". The Swiss franc has not moved yet; traders wonder how liquid a wheel of fondue can be.
